According to the latest IDC report, although Mac shipments fell 11% in the third quarter of 2026, Apple's market share actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5% due to the overall market shipments dropping sharply by 20.1%. Details are as follows.

In a challenging environment, Apple outperformed most of the PC market

IDC today released its third-quarter 2026 global PC shipment report, noting that although Mac shipments declined compared to the previous year, Apple clearly outpaced the overall market.

According to IDC's preliminary data, Apple shipped 5.9 million Macs in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 11.3% from the 6.7 million units shipped in the same period last year.

However, the overall PC market shrank even more significantly, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-over-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

Apple remained the fourth-largest globally, trailing Lenovo. Lenovo took the top spot with 14.9 million units shipped and a 23.8% market share; HP followed closely with 10.3 million units shipped and a 16.5% market share; Dell ranked third with 7.6 million units shipped and a 12.1% market share.

Among the top five vendors, HP suffered the largest year-over-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS had the smallest decline, down 8.6% year-over-year, with shipments of 5.5 million units and a market share of 8.7%.

IDC stated:

Looking ahead, IDC noted that "with elevated inventory and high prices, channel concerns about weak demand may drive promotional activity in the near term," and added that "prices will remain well above historical levels."

The firm also pointed out that the economy has weakened since the previous quarter, which may further dampen demand, making "the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027 more dismal."
